name: Conquerors Who Redrew the World Map
description: From the Persian kings and Alexander to Genghis Khan and Napoleon: the generals and rulers whose armies changed borders and the course of history.

checkpoints.name: The first empires
checkpoints.note: Sargon, the Egyptian pharaohs, the Persian kings and Alexander show how one ruler and one army can bring many peoples under a single throne.

checkpoints.name: Rome, Huns and caliphs
checkpoints.note: Qin Shi Huang unites China, the Maurya Empire spreads across India after Alexander's death, Hannibal leads Carthage against Rome and Caesar conquers Gaul for Rome, and Attila and Arab commanders challenge the old powers.

checkpoints.name: Medieval conquerors
checkpoints.note: Charlemagne, William, Saladin and the Mongols under Genghis, Kublai and Timur build or break kingdoms across Europe and Asia.

checkpoints.name: Gunpowder and new worlds
checkpoints.note: Mehmed, Cortes, Pizarro, Suleiman and Akbar use cannon and discipline to build empires in the Middle East, the Americas and South Asia, while Pachacuti makes the Inca a great Andean empire without gunpowder.

checkpoints.name: Shaka and Napoleon
checkpoints.note: In Europe, Napoleon reshapes the continent in a decade of war ending at Waterloo, while in Africa Shaka builds the Zulu kingdom.
